thread:
maria: quick heads-up — PR #25488 is ready for final approvals. It changes fallback routing to prefer the quantized low-cost model variant when Dedicated capacity is constrained. CI is green. link: https://git.redwood/inference/pull/25488
leo: thanks — which teams do you need? runtime + infra + security?
sanjay: I can take infra eyes after 2pm PT today, fyi. scope?
maria: yes runtime, infra, and security. touches: eviction policy, routing table, and a small KMS metadata flag. risk = possible 99p latency regression if kernel selection flips incorrectly. i added a perf run in the PR description.
olivia: security quick check — is this changing any key material handling or auth flows? if yes i need a short note.
maria: no key rotation, just propagating a metadata flag to VPC deployments for metrics. KMS callsites unchanged. i'll add a one-paragraph note.
jonas: runtime heads-up: the fallback priority logic affects continuous batching behavior. request one extra unit test around eviction thresholds and please re-run the perf harness with long-tail sequences.
maria: ok will add test and re-run perf. the harness command I used: 
```
./scripts/perf/run.sh --suite=eviction --duration=600 --concurrency=8
```
should we capture the 99th pct with trace enabled?
jonas: yes please capture traces and attach the flamegraph. also include kernel selection stats (count per kernel).
deploy-bot: CI: all checks passed for PR #25488 (build, lint, unit, integration) — 1717504980
security-bot: SCA scan: no critical findings. dependency check OK. — 1717505042
maria: pushed test + perf traces, added a short security note in PR description: "no KMS changes; metadata propagation only". re-ran CI.
deploy-bot: CI: re-run passed for PR #25488 — 1717505722
sanjay: skimmed the infra changes — eviction header and header propagation look fine. one nit: can you add a comment explaining TTL units? otherwise lgtm from infra.
maria: added comment about TTL units (ms -> seconds conversion). thanks.
leo: for scheduling — ops prefers canary in their 10am PT slot tomorrow. does that work with runtime? we'll hold merge until canary window reserved.
jonas: 10am PT works for runtime team. after canary stabilizes we'll promote.
olivia: security approves after reading the note and seeing SCA pass. approving here. :thumbsup:
maria: adding the KMS doc link for record: https://docs.redwood/ops/kms-usage#no-rotation-required
jonas: perf numbers look stable: baseline 99p=420ms, after change 99p=435ms (within SLA), kernel distribution unchanged. runtime approves.
sanjay: infra approves.
leo: merging hold removed; i'll queue this for the morning merge window and ping ops for canary.
maria: thanks all — i'll tag ops and the canary monitor, and follow up after the first 30m. tagging: @ops, plan: canary 10am PT, 15m initial ramp, kill-switch ready.
leo: thanks team, appreciate the quick turnaround.
maria: merging tomorrow morning and will post results in #incidents if anything odd shows up. :rocket:
